mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week rebound in RETAIL_REC at t-0w, following a multi-week decline, indicates a renewed consumer willingness to engage in retail and recreation activities, driving further recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, or fails to show a sustained increase from the t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: A strong week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility, as observed at t-0w, signals a broader trend of increased outdoor activity and leisure, which will spill over into retail and recreation spending within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent two weeks despite PARKS showing a week-on-week rise greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and increase in WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w indicates a shift away from home-based activities towards out-of-home work and other engagements, which will directly boost retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES increasing and RESIDENTIAL decreasing in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w, following previous declines, suggests an easing of public health restrictions or a return-to-office mandate, which will sustain increased out-of-home activity and drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, or if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility decline again in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If the recent positive trend in WORKPLACES mobility fails to sustain and drops back into negative territory in the immediate next week, it signals a lack of sustained economic activity that will cause RETAIL_REC to decline over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below 0 after a positive week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the next week, despite WORKPLACES falling below 0 after a positive week.

mechanism_narrative: The strong rebound in GROCERY_PHARM mobility at t-0w, reaching its highest point in the last four weeks, indicates a general increase in essential out-of-home trips, which often precedes or coincides with increased discretionary retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next two weeks, despite GROCERY_PHARM showing a strong rebound at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent rebound in TRANSIT and PARKS mobility at t-0w suggests a broader return to public spaces and leisure activities, indicating increased foot traffic and engagement that will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and PARKS showing a rebound at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated (above 5% from baseline) for two consecutive weeks, it indicates a persistent preference for home-based activities or lingering caution, which will suppress the recovery of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 5% for two consecutive weeks.
